field_changes.before: Draft ordinance amending the Dover Code to add a 'Large Energy Use Facility' moratorium, sponsored by Councilwoman Donyale Hall and Councilman David Anderson; heard by the Council Committee of the Whole (Legislative, Finance and Administration Committee) on 2026-09-15, which recommended forwarding it to full Council and the Planning Commission for review. No ordinance number assigned; the city's official Ordinances/Resolutions register lists nothing past Ordinance 2026-13 (adopted 2026-08-10) as of 2026-09-23. Later retained city materials identify proposed Ordinance 2026-14; its action history lists a September 28 first reading and an October 12 scheduled final reading.
field_changes.after: Ordinance 2026-14, reproduced as adopted in official October12,2026 Council minutes pages41-43, following September28 first reading. Section3 states immediate effect upon adoption. The dated adoption minutes supersede the older undated register status as evidence of the October12 action. The minutes include a mayoral approval statement on page44 but no handwritten execution signatures; separate signed/enrolled copy and later actions are not established.

field_changes.before: Pending as of 2026-09-23. The draft ordinance would immediately suspend the City's acceptance, processing, review, approval, and issuance of permits, site plan approvals, conditional-use approvals, rezonings, subdivision approvals, building permits, utility service agreements, and certificates of occupancy for any new 'Large Energy Use Facility' (a facility using 75+ MW at 85%+ load factor, 100+ MW instantaneous demand, or 30+ MW and NAICS 518210) for 18 months, with exemptions for government/hospital/university/public-safety/clean-hydrogen facilities and small expansions. First proposed publicly in August 2026 (a City Council committee voted unanimously to advance a draft to full Council); the Council Committee of the Whole heard the finalized ordinance text on 2026-09-15 and recommended it go to full Council and the Planning Commission, but no first or final reading before full Council, and no ordinance number, had been recorded as of 2026-09-23. A sponsor's public social-media post described the proposal as a 24-month moratorium, which conflicts with the 18-month term stated in the drafted ordinance text reviewed here; the ordinance text is treated as authoritative. Later retained evidence conflicts: the city register captured 2026-11-05 lists Ordinance 2026-14 as pending, while WBOC reported on 2026-10-12 that Council passed an 18-month pause. Formal adoption and current force remain unresolved.
field_changes.after: Official October12,2026 minutes record adoption of Ordinance2026-14 by unanimous roll call, Sudler absent. The reproduced text immediately pauses acceptance, processing, review and listed approvals for new Large Energy Use Facilities: at least75MW monthly maximum demand with at least85% load factor; at least100MW monthly instantaneous demand; or a defined NAICS518210 data center using or capable of using at least30MW monthly maximum demand. Complete pre-effective applications are stayed unless withdrawn; limited vested-right/takings exemptions require Council approval following City Manager recommendation. Section5 exempts listed public/institutional uses, existing industrial expansions below20% demand, routine maintenance, existing telecommunications, defined clean-hydrogen production and public-utility infrastructure. The term is18months unless sooner repealed, extendable by ordinance. This establishes the historical action/text, not uninterrupted current force; subsequent council actions, litigation and separate executed-copy verification remain open.

field_changes.before: Introduced proposal would require standard tariffs offered after March 14, 2026 to large-load customers to reimburse all reasonably allocable project costs whether or not service is taken in the anticipated amount and time; cap certain basic-rate increases using national energy price changes; restrict recovery of specified political and other expenses; and urge assignment of a 2026 interim tracker study.
field_changes.after: Failed introduced proposal: large-load class covers one customer or up to four customers requesting aggregate new/additional demand exceeding the lesser of 5% of the utility’s three-year average peak demand or 150 MW. Standard tariffs offered after March 14, 2026 would require reimbursement of all reasonably allocable project costs even if anticipated service is not taken. The LSA introduced fiscal note describes this as replacing an at-least-80% reimbursement requirement; this is proposed change analysis, not proof of current law. Other provisions would cap certain basic-rate increases, restrict recovery of specified political/other expenses, and urge a 2026 interim tracker study. The generic load class and fiscal note do not independently establish a qualifying data-center application.
